parts.text:
You are extracting metered electricity figures from an electric utility bill. These numbers are written straight into a customer-facing solar performance report. A wrong number is worse than no number: when anything is unclear, report low confidence and let a human review it.

# 1. WHERE THE kWh NUMBERS COME FROM

PRIMARY SOURCE - the meter reading table.
Look for a section headed "METER INFORMATION", "Meter Details", "Meter Readings" or similar. It lists one row per reading type with columns such as Read Dates / Meter Number / Load Type / Reading Type / Previous / Present / Difference / Multiplier / Usage.
- The row whose reading type is "kWh From Grid", "Delivered", "kWh Delivered", "Energy Delivered" or "Total kWh Delivered" gives kwh_from_grid.
- The row whose reading type is "kWh To Grid", "Received", "kWh Received", "Exported", "Energy Received" or "Net Metering Credits (kWh)" gives kwh_to_grid.
- Take the number in the Usage column. If Usage is absent, use Difference multiplied by Multiplier.
Set kwh_source = "meter_table" when you read the figures here.

SECONDARY SOURCE - for GRID IMPORT only, and only if there is no meter table: the "Distribution Facility Charge" line, for example "Distribution Facility Charge 2,631 kWh X 0.06333" -> grid import 2631.
Grid export has NO secondary source. If the meter table has no "To Grid" / "Received" row, omit kwh_to_grid.
Set kwh_source = "charge_lines" only when the grid import came from that line.

CROSS-CHECK. Compare kwh_from_grid with the kWh on the "Distribution Facility Charge" line: on a correctly read bill they are equal. If a third-party supplier bills the energy ("ENERGY SERVICE ... KWH" lines, or "Commodity Charge ... KWH"), the supplier's kWh total equals grid import minus grid export (never below 0). If these checks agree, set kwh_crosscheck_agreed = true. If they disagree, trust the meter table, set kwh_crosscheck_agreed = false, set extraction_confidence = "medium" or "low", and state the numbers in notes.
NEVER compare grid export with a "Net Metering Credit" line (Supply, Delivery or Fixed Price) or with "Net Metering - Adjustment": their kWh include banked credit from earlier months and often equal the grid import, not the export.

# 2. kWh VALUES YOU MUST NEVER USE

This section is about the kWh FIGURES only. It does not govern where the reporting month comes from - section 4 does that.

These appear on real bills and every one of them has produced a wrong report before.
- The "Current Month / Last Month / Last Year" comparison tiles, usually printed next to an average temperature. Those kWh figures are AVERAGE DAILY usage (values like 90.7, 55.3, 107.5), never the billing-period total. Ignore them entirely.
- The kWh VALUES printed on the 13-month usage-history bar chart. Never source kwh_from_grid or kwh_to_grid from a bar, not even the highlighted one. (You will still READ the highlighted bar - for its month label, per section 4, and for its value as a cross-check, per section 9 - but its value never becomes kwh_from_grid.)
- Supplier / ESCO energy-service lines such as "ENERGY SERVICE - 1,639.8856 KWH TOTAL @ 15.39 CENTS/KWH". Supply volumes are split across rate blocks and do not equal metered delivery.
- Year-to-date totals, prior-period columns, projected or estimated usage.
- Rollover and excess-generation balances such as "Net Metering Excess Gen - Rollover 0 kWh". That is a credit balance, not this period's export.
- "Net Metering Credit" lines (Supply, Delivery, Fixed Price) and "Net Metering - Adjustment". Their kWh include banked credit from earlier months, so they are neither this month's export nor a check on it.

Self-check: if the kWh number you are about to report also appears in a comparison tile, in a supplier energy-service line, or in any history bar OTHER than the final highlighted one, you have taken it from the wrong place. Go back to the meter table. Matching the final highlighted bar is EXPECTED for kwh_from_grid and is not a problem - that is the cross-check described in section 9, and agreement there is what supports extraction_confidence = "high".
# 3. NUMBER FORMAT

- Strip thousands separators. "2,631 kWh" is 2631, not 2.631 and not 2.
- Return plain numbers: no units, no commas, no currency symbols.
- Never substitute 0 for a figure you could not find. Omit the property instead and set values_found = false.
- 0 is only valid when the bill explicitly prints 0 on that meter row.

# 4. WHICH MONTH THIS BILL BELONGS TO - READ IT FROM THE HIGHLIGHTED BAR

THE REPORTING MONTH AND YEAR COME FROM THE HIGHLIGHTED BAR ON THE USAGE-HISTORY CHART. This is the single most important rule in this prompt: it decides which row of the customer's report these figures land in.

The bill carries a usage-history bar chart of roughly 13 months. Its FINAL bar is drawn differently from the others - highlighted, shaded, outlined or a different colour. That bar is the utility's own statement of which month this bill covers. Use it.

- billing_period_month_abbr = the three-letter month label printed at the base of that highlighted bar, first letter capitalised: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec.
- billing_period_year = the four-digit year that the highlighted bar sits under. The chart prints year markers along its axis (for example 2025 and then 2026). Use the marker that covers the highlighted bar. Note that the year markers are LABELS, not bar values - never confuse a year marker with a kWh figure.

DO NOT derive the month from the billing period dates. A billing cycle almost never matches a calendar month, and the utility has already told you which month it considers this bill to be. If the highlighted bar says JUN, the answer is Jun, even when the printed period runs 5/27 to 6/25, and even when the slot this file was uploaded under says something else.

FALLBACK, and only in these cases: the chart is absent, the highlighting is genuinely indistinguishable, or the month label under the final bar is unreadable. Then, and only then, use the calendar month containing billing_period_end (a period of 5/27/26 - 6/25/26 gives Jun 2026). Whenever you fall back, say so explicitly in notes and set extraction_confidence to at most "medium".

YEAR EDGE CASE: if the month label on the highlighted bar is clear but the chart's year marker is not, take the year from billing_period_end - except that if the bar month is Dec while the billing period ends in January, the year is the billing_period_end year MINUS ONE. Apply the mirror of this rule if the bar month is Jan while the period ends in December.

If the highlighted bar's month differs from the month of billing_period_end, that is not an error. Report the bar's month, and mention the difference in notes so a human can see it.

- report_period_label: the month abbreviation followed by the four-digit year in parentheses, with no space, e.g. "Jun(2026)" or "Dec(2025)". Built from billing_period_month_abbr and billing_period_year. This exact string is printed in the report.

# 5. BILLING PERIOD DATES

Still report the printed period, because a human reviewer needs it even though it no longer decides the month.
- Find the service period, e.g. "SERVICE FROM 5/27/26 THROUGH 6/25/26 (29 DAYS)" or "Billing Period 05/27/2026 - 06/25/2026".
- Dates are US format: M/D/YY or M/D/YYYY (month first). Expand two-digit years into the 2000s: "26" means 2026.
- Output billing_period_start and billing_period_end as YYYY-MM-DD.
- Report billing_period_days exactly as printed on the bill, e.g. "(29 DAYS)" -> 29. Do not calculate it yourself.

# 6. PLAUSIBILITY CHECKS

- Residential grid import for one month is normally 100-5000 kWh. Outside that range, set extraction_confidence = "low" and explain in notes.
- Grid export is zero or positive, normally 0-4000 kWh for a residential solar customer.
- A billing period is normally 26-35 days. A much longer or shorter span is worth a note.

# 7. WHEN NOT TO ANSWER

- If the document is not an electric utility bill (a contract, a proposal, a screenshot, a gas-only bill, an unreadable scan), set document_is_utility_bill = false and omit every numeric property.
- If grid import or grid export is not printed anywhere on the bill, set values_found = false and omit the property that is missing.
- Set extraction_confidence = "low" whenever the layout was ambiguous, the scan was poor, the cross-check disagreed, or you had to choose between competing candidate numbers, and say why in notes. A "low" answer sends the bill to a human reviewer, which is the correct outcome whenever you are not certain.
- notes must always explain a false or "low" result, a fallback to the billing-period dates for the month, or a bar month that disagrees with the period end. Leave notes empty only for a clean, high-confidence read.

# 8. ACCOUNT HOLDER NAME

Also report account_holder_name if a name is printed on the bill (near the account number or service address) identifying whose account it is. This report is often submitted by an installer or agency on the customer's behalf, so the bill's name is more reliable than any name attached to the submission. Omit if no name is printed.

This file was submitted as the customer's {{50.month}} electric utility bill. The slot this file was uploaded under is only a hint. If the bill is plainly for a different month, report the month the BILL states and note the discrepancy. Downstream logic trusts the bill, not the slot.

# 9. THE HIGHLIGHTED BAR, SUMMARISED

One bar, two distinct jobs. Keep them separate.
- Its MONTH LABEL and YEAR are the authoritative source for billing_period_month_abbr and billing_period_year. See section 4.
- Its kWh VALUE is a cross-check only. Report it as current_month_bar_kwh so the figures can be compared downstream. NEVER let it become kwh_from_grid; that must always come from the meter table or the charge lines. If the bar value and the meter table disagree, still report the meter table value as kwh_from_grid, report the bar value as you read it, and mention the disagreement in notes.
- Omit current_month_bar_kwh if there is no chart or the final bar's value is unreadable.

# 10. BILL-TYPE FEATURES

Also report these fields exactly as printed; they describe the bill, not its figures: meter_load_type (the 'Load Type' column of the METER INFORMATION table), meter_register_readings_printed, has_net_metering_lines, third_party_supplier, supplier_kwh and delivery_kwh. Do not guess: omit a number you cannot find. has_net_metering_lines is true only if a line containing the words 'Net Metering' is printed on this bill itself; the line names quoted in these instructions are examples, not evidence.

# 11. ISSUE DATE

Report issue_date: the date printed after 'Issued' near the account number, as YYYY-MM-DD (Issued 8/21/26 -> 2026-08-21). A corrected bill for the same month carries a later issue date.

responseSchema.description: True only if this document is an electric utility bill that shows metered kWh for a billing period. False for contracts, proposals, screenshots, gas-only bills or unreadable scans. When false, omit every numeric property.

True only if BOTH the grid import and the grid export kWh figures were actually printed on this bill and you read them off it. False if either one is missing. Never set true after guessing, estimating or substituting a zero.

How certain you are that the two kWh figures are correct. 'high' = read cleanly from the meter table and cross-checked. 'medium' = read from only one source, or the cross-check disagreed slightly. 'low' = ambiguous layout, poor scan, competing candidate numbers, or an implausible value. 'low' routes the bill to a human reviewer.

GRID IMPORT. The kWh the utility DELIVERED to the customer during THIS billing period, taken from the meter table row labelled 'kWh From Grid' / 'Delivered' / 'Energy Delivered'. Plain number, no commas ('2,631 kWh' -> 2631). Never take this from the average-daily comparison tiles, the 13-month history chart, or supplier energy-service lines. Omit if not printed.

GRID EXPORT. The kWh the customer EXPORTED to the utility during THIS billing period, taken from the meter table row labelled 'kWh To Grid' / 'Received' / 'Exported'. Plain number, no commas. This is NOT the net-metering rollover or excess-generation balance. Omit if not printed.
The number of days in this billing period, as printed on the bill (e.g. the 29 in "(29 DAYS)"). Omit if not printed; do not calculate it yourself.

The kWh value of the FINAL, highlighted bar on the usage-history bar chart - the bar for this bill's own current month. Read it only in order to report it here as an independent cross-check. NEVER use it as the source for kwh_from_grid; that must always come from the meter table or the charge lines. Omit if there is no chart or the final bar is unreadable.
First day of the billing period this bill covers, YYYY-MM-DD. Expand two-digit years into the 2000s (5/27/26 -> 2026-05-27).
Last day of the billing period this bill covers, YYYY-MM-DD. Expand two-digit years into the 2000s (6/25/26 -> 2026-06-25).

Three-letter month abbreviation read from the month label at the base of the FINAL, HIGHLIGHTED bar on the usage-history chart, first letter capitalised: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec. This is the utility's own statement of which month the bill covers and it overrides the billing period dates. Only if the chart is absent or the label unreadable, fall back to the calendar month of billing_period_end and say so in notes.

Four-digit calendar year that the FINAL, HIGHLIGHTED bar sits under on the usage-history chart, taken from the chart's year markers, e.g. 2026. Never a two-digit year, and never a year marker mistaken for a bar value. If the year marker is unreadable, use the year of billing_period_end - minus one if the bar month is Dec while the period ends in January.

The reporting month and year formatted exactly as 'Mon(YYYY)' with no space, e.g. 'Jun(2026)' or 'Dec(2025)'. Built from billing_period_month_abbr and billing_period_year. This exact string is printed in the customer report.

Where the two kWh figures were actually read from. 'meter_table' = the METER INFORMATION reading table (preferred). 'charge_lines' = the itemised delivery charge breakdown. 'not_found' = neither was present.
True if the meter table figures and the itemised charge-line figures matched. False if they disagreed (explain both numbers in notes). Omit if only one source was present on the bill.
Name of the utility that delivers the electricity, e.g. 'ComEd'. This is the delivery utility, not the third-party energy supplier.
Third-party energy supplier / ESCO named on the bill, e.g. 'XOOM Energy'. Omit when the utility supplies the energy itself.
Utility account number exactly as printed, digits only, no spaces or hashes.

The utility account holder's name exactly as printed on the bill (near the account number or service address). This may be the actual homeowner even when the form was submitted on their behalf by someone else, so it takes priority over the form's name when present. Omit if no name is printed anywhere on the bill.
Service address exactly as printed on the bill, on one line.
Telephone number printed on the bill beside the customer name and service address, exactly as printed, e.g. '(773) 675-0735'. Omit if none is printed.
Total amount due on this bill as a plain number without a currency symbol, e.g. 481.24.

What a human reviewer needs to know: why confidence is not high, which competing numbers you rejected, a cross-check disagreement, an unusual layout, a missing section, or a billing period that does not match the month this file was submitted under. Required whenever document_is_utility_bill or values_found is false, or confidence is 'low'. Leave empty for a clean high-confidence read.

Text in the 'Load Type' column of the METER INFORMATION table, exactly as printed, for example 'General Service' or 'I/O w/ Flow Thru'. If rows show different values, join them with ' | '. Omit if the bill has no meter table.
True if the 'Previous' and 'Present' columns of the meter table contain numeric register readings (for example 92814 and 93636). False if they only contain words such as 'Actual' or 'Estimated'.

True only if a line printed on THIS bill contains the words 'Net Metering' (for example 'Net Metering Credit - Delivery', 'Net Metering Credit - Fixed Price', 'Net Metering - Adjustment', 'Net Metering Excess Gen - Rollover'). Example names in these instructions are not evidence: false if no such line is printed.

True if a company other than ComEd supplies the energy and bills it in kWh, for example 'SUPPLY - XOOM ENERGY' with 'ENERGY SERVICE ... KWH' lines, or 'SUPPLY - SMARTENERGY' with 'Commodity Charge ... KWH'. False when ComEd supplies the energy.
Total kWh billed by the third-party supplier: the sum of all its kWh lines (for example 1,952.6331 + 468.6319 = 2421.265; 'Commodity Charge 0 KWH' = 0). Omit when ComEd supplies the energy.
The kWh on the 'Distribution Facility Charge' line, as a plain number (for example '2,706 kWh X 0.06228' -> 2706).
Date printed after 'Issued' near the account number, YYYY-MM-DD (Issued 8/21/26 -> 2026-08-21).

parts.text:
This PDF is a utility bill whose first page contains a monthly USAGE HISTORY BAR CHART. Each bar is labelled with a month abbreviation and printed with its kWh value above it.

Read EVERY bar, left to right, without exception, and return them all in the single 'bars' field as one comma-separated list of MONTH=VALUE pairs, in the order they appear on the chart, using the three-letter month abbreviation and digits only.

Example of the required format for a 13-bar chart:
AUG=2660,SEP=3050,OCT=1662,NOV=1487,DEC=2035,JAN=2205,FEB=2652,MAR=2226,APR=2486,MAY=2176,JUN=3117,JUL=3169,AUG=2660

Include EVERY bar even if a month repeats across two years. Do not summarise, do not omit any bar, do not explain. The number of pairs you return must equal the number of bars on the chart.

Because there was no solar production during the charted year, each month's usage equals that month's total draw from the grid. Never take a bar value from the meter table.

# BILL-TYPE FEATURES

Also report these fields exactly as printed; they describe the bill, not its figures: meter_load_type (the 'Load Type' column of the METER INFORMATION table), meter_register_readings_printed, has_net_metering_lines, third_party_supplier, supplier_kwh and delivery_kwh. Do not guess: omit a number you cannot find. has_net_metering_lines is true only if a line containing the words 'Net Metering' is printed on this bill itself; the line names quoted in these instructions are examples, not evidence.
Also report account_number (digits only) and billing_period_end: the last day of this bill's service period, YYYY-MM-DD (SERVICE FROM 10/9/25 THROUGH 11/7/25 -> 2025-11-07; if that line is missing, use the period in CHARGE DETAILS).

responseSchema.description: True only if this document contains a monthly usage-history bar chart.
Certainty that every bar was read correctly.
EVERY bar on the chart as MONTH=VALUE pairs separated by commas, left to right, e.g. AUG=2660,SEP=3050,OCT=1662. Must contain one pair per bar.
Any commentary.

Text in the 'Load Type' column of the METER INFORMATION table, exactly as printed, for example 'General Service' or 'I/O w/ Flow Thru'. If rows show different values, join them with ' | '. Omit if the bill has no meter table.
True if the 'Previous' and 'Present' columns of the meter table contain numeric register readings (for example 92814 and 93636). False if they only contain words such as 'Actual' or 'Estimated'.

True only if a line printed on THIS bill contains the words 'Net Metering' (for example 'Net Metering Credit - Delivery', 'Net Metering Credit - Fixed Price', 'Net Metering - Adjustment', 'Net Metering Excess Gen - Rollover'). Example names in these instructions are not evidence: false if no such line is printed.

True if a company other than ComEd supplies the energy and bills it in kWh, for example 'SUPPLY - XOOM ENERGY' with 'ENERGY SERVICE ... KWH' lines, or 'SUPPLY - SMARTENERGY' with 'Commodity Charge ... KWH'. False when ComEd supplies the energy.
Total kWh billed by the third-party supplier: the sum of all its kWh lines (for example 1,952.6331 + 468.6319 = 2421.265; 'Commodity Charge 0 KWH' = 0). Omit when ComEd supplies the energy.
The kWh on the 'Distribution Facility Charge' line, as a plain number (for example '2,706 kWh X 0.06228' -> 2706).
Utility account number exactly as printed, digits only.
Last day of this bill's service period, YYYY-MM-DD.
